title: 3am signal annotator - candidate sketch
body:
Quick late-night brain dump after candidate loop (senior runtime engineer). Do not trust as polished feedback — this is raw, biased, and timeboxed to 20–30m.

Context: took the candidate through a micro-case (KV cache correctness + eviction tradeoffs) and a system-design whiteboard (multi-tenant scheduling / routing). Small pairing session on a tiny kernel-level latency regression reproduce.

High-level gut: capable engineer, thoughtful about edge cases, but a few redflags around scope discipline and optimistic timelines. Good debates on tradeoffs but sometimes tries to solve for perfect correctness at cost of pragmatic ship-ability.

Detailed notes (chronological):
- Intro / culture fit (5m): relaxed, asked clear questions about team goals and observability. Mentions prior infra at a fintech scale — solid ops background.
- Micro-case (20m):
  - Prompt: implement a small API that keeps a fixed-size KV cache with async persistence. Evaluate correctness under concurrency.
  - Approach: sketched a ReadWriteLock + background flush thread. Brought up CAS and compare-exchange for safe updates.
  - Strengths shown: recognized write amplification, suggested batching writes and TTL-based lazy flushing.
  - Misses: didn't initially call out backpressure or bounded task queue semantics for the flush worker — we probed and they iterated.
  - Implementation sketch: pseudocode for lock + queue, mentioned optimistic locking for hot keys.
  - Note: when asked about eviction policy under heavy tail load, proposed LRU w/ segments; didn't mention approximate LFU or TinyLFU, but rationale for segmented LRU was sound.

- Whiteboard (30m): multi-tenant routing and graceful degradation
  - Good idea: per-tenant async priority buckets + fast-path for small requests.
  - Brought up region-aware routing and cold-start of model shards.
  - Missed an end-to-end SLO budget model (didn't quantify percent of degraded traffic acceptable), but recovered with a back-of-envelope calculation when prompted.
  - Proposes circuit-breaker style fallback to smaller quantized model on overload — practical and aligned with Redwood thesis.

- Pair debugging (25m): reproduced a 3–5% tail-latency regression on a toy harness
  - Candidate used printf-style tracing to narrow to KV cache lock contention. Implemented a quick experiment swapping coarse RW lock for per-shard mutex -> latency improved.
  - Strength: executes quickly in the loop, incremental experiments, good use of metrics.
  - Weakness: left race condition in demo commit (caught later) — tells me sometimes misses a final safety sweep under time pressure.

Strengths summary:
- Systems intuition: strong; knows tradeoffs between latency and consistency.
- Debugging: pragmatic, quick experiments, comfortable on the command line.
- Architecture: sensible proposals, aligns with product constraints (cost/latency).

Risks / concerns:
- Scope discipline: leans toward elegant but complex designs; might over-engineer early iterations.
- QA under pressure: missed a race in the demo; could improve small safety checks during pairing.
- Unclear experience with our specific serving stack (gRPC endpoint tuning, kv-shard invariants, our custom batching heuristic) — comfortable in principle but will need ramp on infra specifics.

Score (structured, quick):
- Technical (systems + coding): 7/10 — solid, can contribute immediately to debugging and architecture.
- Ownership / pragmatism: 6/10 — good instincts, needs reminders to favor incremental shipping.
- Communication / collaboration: 8/10 — clear, asked good questions, receptive to feedback.
- Role fit (senior runtime): 7/10 overall.

Suggested next steps / hire recommendation: hire-with-conditions. Recommend advancing to manager panel and org-fit interview, with a short pairing follow-up focused on small-scope deliverables (i.e., give a realistic 2–3 day spike: produce an incremental change to a ref-counted cache with a benchmark and safety tests). If they can show pragmatic tradeoffs and safety checks in that follow-up, strong buy.

Open questions to verify in follow-up:
- How do they prioritize when a shipping date conflicts with an ideal design? Concrete example.
- Ask for a code sample or walkthrough of a production bug they shipped end-to-end in past year — focus on testing and rollback story.
- Clarify experience with language runtimes we use (Rust in hot paths vs. Python orchestration).

Quick action items for hiring pool:
- Add flagged note "needs pragmatic-scope-check" on candidate profile (INF-HIRE tag).
- Assign a two-hour pairing follow-up with infra owner (Maya) next week; outline: small benchmarked change + test.
- Send this raw note to hiring thread and recommend the manager panel.

Notes to self: I keep thinking they could be a strong contributor for infra resilience work if we help temper scope. Would prefer A/B with another finalist who is stronger on disciplined ship cadence.

End of dump. Will refine into a formal passback if we move forward.
